Internal: ability to cope with stressors, religious beliefs, frustration tolerance

While confidentiality is important to facilitate a climate of trust within the patient/client relationship, there are limits to confidentiality that the patient must be informed of in the beginning of the treatment.
PROF: There should always be a strong presumption to respect confidentiality and avoid breaking confidences when at all possible.

However, there are three universal situations where clinicians are mandated to break confidentiality and have a duty to inform:
Clinicians have a duty to report abuse.  If the patient discloses that they are a victim of abuse, confidentiality will be broken.  Additionally if it is disclosed that a child under the age of 18 is being abused, anyone over the age of 60 is being abused, and anyone, of any age, that has a disability is being abused, confidentiality will be broken and the abuse reported.
Clinicians have a duty to protect patients from committing suicide.
Clinicians have a duty to warn and protect intended victims of homicide.
However, because Taylor is 13 years old, many providers may break confidentiality and inform her parents of her self-injury.
The clearest situations in which confidentiality is broken are those in which the patient places self or another person at significant risk of serious harm.
